title: The North Face Meso 22 review: a light two-person tent that held in Death Valley wind
dek: A sub-4-pound, three-pole tent with 8.5 mm DAC Featherlite poles. Owners report it held in 50+ mph gusts. It's best for one person, or two who don't mind closeness.
subject: The North Face Meso 22
verdict: The Meso 22 is a light, compact backpacking tent that owners say is waterproof and wind-stable, including 50+ mph gusts in Death Valley. It fits two snugly and one with room for gear. Add extra stakes, because the fly needs more stake-out points than the tent comes with.
bestFor: Solo backpackers who want room for gear, or couples comfortable in a snug tent.
notFor: Two tall adults who want headroom on both sides.
pros: Owner reports it held in 50+ mph gusts and rain
Many fly stake points for stability
Packs small enough for a 40 L pack with gear
cons: Roof shape gives less headroom on one side
Comes with too few stakes for all the fly points
Gear on the exposed side of the fly needs protecting
body:
## The short version

The Meso 22 is a light, three-pole, two-person backpacking tent. Its poles are thinner than most North Face tents of the era, at 8.5 mm, which helps keep the trail weight around 3 pounds 12 ounces. Owners on Trailspace describe it as a strong performer for the money.

## Weather

One owner reports it held up wonderfully in 50+ mph gusts and rain in Death Valley. Both reviewers describe it as waterproof, and the fly has many staking points that keep it stable once they're all used.

## Space

Opinions depend on who's inside. A 6-foot-2 solo user found plenty of room for gear. A 6-foot-2 owner and his 5-foot-5 wife sleep comfortably in it together at 32°F. The roof design leaves less headroom on one side, and gear stored under the fly on the exposed side needs covering to stay dry.

## Setup and packing

Owners call it quick to pitch and take down. It packs small enough that one owner fits it in a 40-liter pack with two to four days of gear.

## What to fix

Owners point out two things: the plastic window in the fly, and too few stakes. The fly needs about four more stake points than the included stakes cover, so bring extras.

## Poles and parts

The Meso 22 uses **3 poles**, **8.5 mm** tubing, **DAC Featherlite**.

At 8.5 mm, Meso poles are thinner than the 9 mm poles used in most North Face tents of the same era, so a 9 mm pole won't be an exact match even if the length is right.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Meso 22 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Meso%2022), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

For solo trips or a couple who don't mind closeness, the Meso 22 is a light, weather-tough tent. Carry extra stakes and you'll get the most out of it.
